proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~5 eV), electronically insulating oxide that is chemically compatible with both the LiCoO2 cathode and the sulfide electrolyte. Its phosphate framework is reported to suppress sulfide oxidation and cathode-side interdiffusion, so it should give a low interfacial reaction penalty at 4.0 V.

LiF is a wide-gap, electrochemically robust fluoride that is fully lithiated and oxidation-resistant at about 4 V vs Li. Its reduced, fluoride-rich chemistry should avoid the P-O/S-O reaction products seen with Li3PO4 when in contact with the sulfide electrolyte, which may lower the interfacial reaction penalty.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaauhx) was insulating and wide-gap but still gave a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/atom, with the sulfide contact forming P2O5, SCl4 and SO2. This suggests a different anion chemistry may be needed, so I am testing a fluoride family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, insulating lithium oxide with Zr4+ in a highly stable oxidation state. Zr-O bonds are hard to reduce by the sulfide electrolyte, so the reduction and anion-exchange products seen with Li3PO4 (P2O5, SO2) and LiF (LiPF6, S) may be less favorable. Its oxide chemistry differs from the phosphate and halide families already tested.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (penalty 0.337, bin 16) and LiF (penalty 0.310, bin 15) both gave contact reaction penalties above the 0.05 eV acceptance threshold. proposal.hypothesis: Li4SiO4 is a fully lithiated orthosilicate with Si4+ in its highest stable oxidation state, so it should resist reduction by the sulfide electrolyte. Its Li-rich composition offers little driving force for Li exchange with Li6PS5Cl or LiCoO2, and its wide gap should keep it insulating. Silicates have not yet been tested, and the phosphate, halide and Zr-oxide families all gave penalties above 0.3 eV/atom.
proposal.motivation: Earlier contacts with Li3PO4 (0.337, bin 16), LiF (0.310, bin 15) and Li2ZrO3 (0.574, bin 28) all showed sulfide-driven reaction products, so the next test is a different, Si4+-based oxide family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a fully lithiated, wide-gap oxide with no reducible cation.
